diagnostic_image_plan.target: show bract tier above or below scape midpoint
compare degree and pattern of division
confirm petaloid sepals; color is not decisive

learner_visual_status.note: One verified exact-species photo is a temporary anchor; diagnostic bract-tier photos remain priority.

taxonomic_note: Accepted Anemone caroliniana Walter (1788). Anemone caroliniana Torr. & A.Gray (1838) is an illegitimate later homonym mapped to A. berlandieri, NOT to this accepted species.
look_here_first: Look at the entire flowering scape: ONE tier of three involucral bracts sits BELOW the midpoint. Examine multiple basal leaves: at least one is divided similarly to the involucral bracts. Confirm the bract tier and leaf relationship before using the flower.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Master Plant Pool row 72, 1 source flag; reviewed taxonomy/diagnostics dated 2026-10-09
project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO/FNA accept species and support Texas nativity at state scale; three target-zone county proofs not established. No confirmed-target-native metric credit.

morphology_keys.habit: Low spring-flowering herbaceous perennial from a short tuber-like rhizome; solitary flower on a scape.
morphology_keys.leaves: Basal leaves deeply divided; at least one basal leaf resembles the involucral bracts in division.
morphology_keys.involucre: One tier of leaflike bracts BELOW midpoint of flowering scape; inspect whole scape for accurate position.
morphology_keys.flower: One terminal flower with numerous narrow petaloid sepals; color varies and is not a safe separator.
morphology_keys.fruit: Aggregate achene head; obtain a mature close-up when possible for confirmation.
best_field_traits: one involucral-bract tier BELOW scape midpoint
at least one basal leaf divided similarly to bracts
solitary spring flower with petaloid sepals
often found in sandy habitats, but habitat is supporting only

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. berlandieri has one bract tier ABOVE midpoint and all basal leaves dissimilar to the bracts. A. edwardsiana has TWO bract tiers. Flower color and sepal number alone are unreliable.
